answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to lock a deposit before it can earn trust-weighted rewards. After a zephyr of suspicious trades, peers can challenge an agent with evidence of duplicated control; a successful challenge slashes its stake and redistributes part to the challenger. This does not prove one human per identity, but forces a Sybil attacker to fund every persona separately and risk losing those deposits, making a large fake fleet expensive to sustain across a long voyage through the canyon of scrutiny.
